html: The Aparai, also written Apalaí, are a Carib-speaking people of the north-eastern Amazon in Pará, Brazil, living along the Paru de Leste river near the borders of Suriname and French Guiana. For more than a century they have lived closely with the Wayana, sharing villages and marrying between the groups. They farm cassava, fish and hunt, and are known for featherwork, basketry and painted pottery. Disease cut their numbers steeply in the 1900s; they have since recovered, and their villages lie in protected Indigenous lands near the Tumucumaque mountains.
